commit_message:
[Merged] Add an experimental fix to avoid attempting to mmap memory from an offset that is not a multiple of the system page size on systems with page sizes larger than 32KB.

FossilOrigin-Name: 6f3a5c24d254fc6faf607b505bdef4a7aafc21af
pr_title: Support page-aligned WAL shared-memory mappings with 64-bit size arithmetic
pr_description:
Group WAL shared-memory regions into mappings aligned to the system page size, including systems with pages larger than 32 KB. Use 64-bit arithmetic for the affected Unix and Windows shared-memory sizes, page counters, and offsets, and update the Windows size trace format.

Validation: git diff --check passed, and the PR state applies cleanly against the parent snapshot.

ground_truth.reason: This PR includes the feature with the fix already applied, so the vulnerability is not present

intro_commit_message:
Add an experimental fix to avoid attempting to mmap memory from an offset that is not a multiple of the system page size on systems with page sizes larger than 32KB.

FossilOrigin-Name: 6f3a5c24d254fc6faf607b505bdef4a7aafc21af
fix_commit_message:
Fix the VFSes so that there is no 32-bit integer overflow in the xShmMap method if the WAL file size exceeds about 25 terabytes, or if the header is corrupted to make SQLite think that the WAL file size is that big. [bugs:/info/2026-05-21T03:53:03Z|Bug 2026-05-21T03:53:03Z].

FossilOrigin-Name: 9ac4a33a2932d353c4871fd8e09c10addf827f1fc3fc9380037d738cf2cd0353
agent_reasoning: The region-count and region-size products previously used 32-bit signed integers, allowing large or corrupted WAL metadata to overflow shared-memory byte counts. The source edits reproduce the supplied changes in the older snapshot: widening Unix byte counts, page counters, mapping sizes and indices, and widening the specified Windows size and offset expressions. Only the two VFS source files were edited; tests and repository metadata were left untouched.
